summary: Big improvement: no floor penetration (from 21 frames), a readable contact / absorb / push-off / flight sequence (F000, F003-F004, F006-F007, F008-F009), a 105 deg recovery, pumping elbows and no lockstep. One medium problem is left: the supporting foot skates during push-off and the root rises unevenly into the flight. Everything else is polish (knee accel of 11 deg/frame^2 at toe-off and contact is acceptable for a run).

findings.observation: During push-off the planted toe slides back twice as fast as the rest of the stance: the contact point moves 0.19 studs/frame while the foot is flat (F001-F004 left, F011-F014 right) but 0.41 on F006/F016 and 0.25 on F007/F017 (metrics: stance speed std 0.059, 2 foot_slide_segments). The thigh sweeps 9 deg/frame from F005 to F007 while the foot also whips from 8 to 30 deg of pitch about the ankle. The root also rises unevenly (+0.09, +0.14, +0.05, +0.01 over F004-F008), and the trailing toe is only 0.05 above the floor on F008/F018, so the flight shows on a single frame per step. Fix: a shorter, slower hip extension through push-off (thigh 2 at frame 5, 17 at frame 7), a softer toe roll (ankle -21 at 6, -13 at 7), a slightly higher flight arc, and the stance root re-planted.
